To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the accuracy and precision of the proposed method decrease with the increasing of the nodal spacing, (ii) for the same nodal spacing, the accuracy and precision are better for the cortical than for trabecular bone and (iii) the main source of error is the intrinsic noise of images.
the precision and accuracy errors in the prediction of local zero strains in bovine cortical bone decrease with increasing the region of interest, by following a power law.
the accuracy of the DVC method depends on both the size of the analyzed region and the noise of the images.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of bone tissue at the micro scale.
the development of a new methodology for the measurement of bone strain in three dimensions.
the analysis of bone tissue at the tissue level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the absence of an absolute standard, the best way to evaluate the accuracy of the DVC is to use repeated acquisitions of the same sample.
a compromise between spatial resolution, accuracy of strain measurement and the size of the analyzed region is inevitable.
the accuracy of the method depends on the nodal spacing used and on the size of the volume of interest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DVC method is accurate and robust for the study of bone tissue deformation.
the accuracy and precision of the DVC method is inversely proportional to the nodal spacing.
, for the purpose of strain analysis, the spatial resolution is more important than the accuracy, and it can be increased at the expense of accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of the DVC-based strain analysis of bone samples can be improved by using a larger nodal spacing, but at the expense of spatial resolution.
the accuracy of DVC is not only a function of the image resolution but also of the size of the volume of interest analyzed.
the accuracy and precision of the method is not limited by the intrinsic noise of µCT images, but by the compromise between the spatial resolution and accuracy.
